ladder_entries.boundary_rationale: User-confirmed via listening: there is a repeat of the first introduction at approximately t=17s, matching the metadata-derived hypothesis exactly. Phase 3F.7 analysis had already built strong convergent evidence for this via two independent metadata signals: (1) Onset-gap scan: largest early gaps at t=17.26s (0.647s) and t=35.16s (0.651s), a ~2x relationship. (2) Pitch-class-content scan (2s windows): from t=0-18s, the harmony moves C major (F-natural present, 2-6s) -> G major preparation (F# present, 6-16s) -> tonic-ish (bare C-E-G triad, 18-20s) -- a complete tonic-to-dominant-and-back arc. This exact pattern repeats almost identically from t=20-36s (F-natural 20-24s, F# 24-34s). After t=36s, new pitch-class material appears (Eb/D#, foreign to both C and G major), consistent with a development section beginning. User confirmation now resolves what metadata alone could only suggest -- status upgraded from 'tentative' to 'confirmed'.
ladder_entries.excerpt_note: File as provided is the full first movement (90.47s, 666 notes), not pre-cut to the exposition. A metadata-only gap analysis (largest inter-onset gaps across both hands) found notable pauses at approx. t=17.3s and t=35.2s -- roughly a 2x relationship, consistent with (but not proof of) the exposition being played once (ending ~17.3s) then repeated (ending ~35.2s), with a further gap at ~62.6s possibly marking a later section boundary (development/recapitulation). This is a preliminary, data-informed hypothesis only -- exact_excerpt_end_sec is NOT set from this alone. Recommend a manual listening or score-reference pass (e.g. against a public-domain score/recording) before cutting; if the repeat hypothesis holds, the no-repeat exposition-only excerpt would be approximately [0.0, 17.3]s, but this must be confirmed, not assumed.
